thread:
maria: FYI support escalated — customer acme-corp reports their audit log export to Splunk has been dropping all events for their tenant since 2026-11-02 01:00 UTC. Ticket #INC-12345, P2. They see successful delivery responses from our forwarder but SIEM shows gaps :confused:
liam: Which forwarding path are they using? direct HEC or S3 staging + forward? any sample delivery logs? :eyes:
maria: They're on direct HEC with token auth. Pasted a trimmed forwarder log they attached:
```
[2026-11-02T01:02:14Z] forwarder: POST https://hec.acme-splunk.example/services/collector 200 ok tenant=acme-corp batch_id=987
[2026-11-02T01:03:01Z] forwarder: delivered batch=988 tenant=acme-corp
[2026-11-02T01:03:01Z] forwarder: skippayload tenant=acme-corp reason="authz: envelope_decrypt_failed"
```
ajay: "envelope_decrypt_failed" points to a KMS/HSM envelope decryption error on our side. Did anyone touch the tenant key policy or rotate keys yesterday? I see a KMS policy change applied to the acme-corp key at 2026-11-02T00:55Z in the audit config repo. :thinking_face:
support-eng: SIEM ingestion logs we pulled show that events from that tenant are arriving at our inbound queue but are not being forwarded to HEC — they get dropped after the forwarder attempts to decrypt per-tenant envelopes. Query we ran (splunk): `index=redwood_inbound tenant="acme-corp" | stats count by _time` shows a gap starting 01:00 UTC.
maria: Also worth noting customer changed to use structured events and a new field name: `actor_id` (previously `user_id`). When we do parsing in the forwarder we do a strict schema map — if parser throws we currently drop the event. Example payload they sent that fails parse:
```
{"timestamp":"2026-11-02T01:02:59Z","event_type":"session.login","actor_id":"u-4983","meta":{...}}
```
liam: Two separate failure modes then: (1) KMS decryption errors causing skip, (2) schema mismatch causing parser-drops even if payload decrypted. Repro steps I'd do: run the forwarder locally with DEBUG and `FORWARDER_TENANT=acme-corp`, replay the inbound queue blob for timestamp range 01:00-01:10 UTC, and watch for `envelope_decrypt_failed` and `schema_error` logs. Also check the KMS key id used in the envelope: `envelope.kid`.
katie: What's the quick mitigation for the customer while we investigate? They want events back ASAP.
ajay: Short-term mitigation options (pick one):
- rollback the KMS policy change that removed decrypt permission for the forwarder service principal (we can re-apply policy after).
- enable per-tenant fallback to S3 staging (store raw encrypted payloads to S3 for replay) — but that requires a config flip and may be slower.
I just rolled the KMS policy back for acme-corp at 02:03 UTC (I reverted the commit) — please confirm if forwarder resumes. :white_check_mark:
maria: I asked customer to replay. Support says Splunk shows a partial catch-up after a replay started at 02:10 UTC. They still see parser-related drops for the new `actor_id` field.
liam: For parser-drops we should update the forwarder schema to accept `actor_id` as alias for `user_id` and add a lenient parsing mode for forwarder->SIEM path. I'll open a PR with a quick mapping and a unit test that rejects fewer fields.
support-eng: Confirmed via inbound metrics: events for acme-corp resumed at 02:12 UTC and delivery successes are again present. However, 2,300 events were dropped while the decrypt issue was active. We should offer the customer a replay and explain the root cause.
katie: Action items: ajay to produce a short incident note and link the KMS policy diff (owner), liam to submit parser/alias PR + test (owner), support to coordinate replay and customer comms (owner = support-eng). I'll file the follow-up SLA incident and mark as P1->P2 transition.
maria: Thanks — please also update the runbook (audit-export-runbook) with steps to quickly validate KMS envelope permissions and a checklist to flip to S3-staging fallback. Adding to that: add an observability alert on `envelope_decrypt_failed` rate per-tenant (threshold 5/min) so we catch this earlier.
ajay: Will do. I'll include KMS diff and remediation steps in the postmortem. Also adding a quick smoke test to deployment pipeline that decrypts a sample envelope with each tenant key change.
maria: Closing here after support confirms replay delivered missing events. Customer notified and offered 90-day retention replay window if they want additional backfill. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
